name: Engagement and Therapeutic Relationship Building
description: Therapist establishes a genuine, collaborative relationship with the patient characterized by warmth, empathy, openness, and trust, setting the stage for productive dialogue and intervention.

goal.objective: Build a safe and collaborative therapeutic foundation for intervention.

success_levels.ideal: Patient feels understood, safe, trusting, and actively engaged in the therapy process.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient shows some openness and willingness to participate, even if guarded.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient feels misunderstood, unsafe, withdrawn, or resistant to collaboration.

goal.reward_hint: Patient expresses trust, participates willingly, or positively references the relationship.

states: Initial sessions where rapport must be established
When trust or openness is low or resistance is present
Patient expresses hesitancy, shame, or uncertainty about therapy
Therapeutic progress stalls due to a weak relationship

micro_actions.name: Validate and Empathize
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses verbal affirmations, reflective listening, and empathic responses to validate the patient's feelings, experiences, and distress.
states: Patient expresses emotions (e.g., shame, confusion, fear)
In response to disclosure of painful experiences
Whenever signs of emotional distress or uncertainty arise

micro_actions.name: Ask Open and Curious Questions
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses open-ended questions to show interest in the patient’s perspective and allow free expression, fostering safety and curiosity.
states: Beginning of sessions
When eliciting background or patient concerns
When patient is reluctant or guarded

micro_actions.name: Normalize and Reduce Stigma
micro_actions.description: Therapist offers statements that normalize common difficulties and emotional responses, reducing feelings of shame or isolation.
states: Patient expresses shame, embarrassment, or fear of negative judgment
During discussion of distressing or taboo topics

micro_actions.name: Postpone Challenging Until Rapport is Built
micro_actions.description: Therapist intentionally avoids premature cognitive challenging or guided discovery until sufficient trust and rapport have been established.
states: Early sessions
Signs of hesitancy or emotional vulnerability
When patient signals they are not ready for challenge

micro_actions.name: Invite Feedback on the Relationship
micro_actions.description: Therapist explicitly asks the patient about their comfort with the process, whether they feel understood, and how the relationship feels.
states: Any session where relationship issues or barriers emerge
Therapeutic 'check-in' moments (e.g., mid or late session)

name: Assessment and Cognitive Case Formulation
description: Therapist gathers information, explores patterns, and synthesizes cognitive, emotional, and behavioral data to collaboratively develop a shared understanding of the patient's difficulties using CBT models.

goal.objective: Create an individualized CBT-based formulation that links theory with the patient’s problems and informs targeted intervention.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient share a clear, collaboratively-built formulation aligned with CBT principles, guiding targets for change.
success_levels.acceptable: Basic understanding of presenting problems and some relevant cognitive patterns are established.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No meaningful formulation is constructed; information remains fragmented or unshared.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist and patient verbalize agreement on a case formulation or identify shared goals based on it.

states: Initial therapy sessions when presenting problems and history are unclear
After rapport is established but targets for intervention have not been identified
Complex or intertwined symptom presentations needing clarification

micro_actions.name: Elicit Specific Negative Thoughts and Core Beliefs
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses focused questioning and Socratic prompts to uncover key automatic thoughts, assumptions, and core beliefs linked to presenting problems.
states: Early assessment phase
Whenever patient reports distress or problematic behaviors

micro_actions.name: Distinguish Between Thoughts, Emotions, and Behaviors
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts patient to separate and label their thoughts, emotional states, and consequent behaviors to clarify relationships and patterns.
states: Case formulation discussions
Patient presents complex or overlapping symptoms

micro_actions.name: Rate Mood, Beliefs, and Emotional Responses
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks patient to numerically rate mood, strength of beliefs, or intensity of emotion using scales (0-100%, 1–10) during assessment or prior to interventions.
states: During initial and follow-up interventional planning
Upon identification of target cognitions

micro_actions.name: Explore Patient's History and Symptom Patterns
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks directed questions about the patient’s background, onset and course of symptoms, previous coping responses and experiences.
states: First sessions
Any time the presenting problem is unclear

micro_actions.name: Document Formulation and Collaboratively Review
micro_actions.description: Therapist summarizes the assessment findings, documents them (visually or verbally), and invites collaborative review and agreement from the patient.
states: Following synthesis of cognitive/emotional/behavioral data
Prior to moving to intervention planning

name: Psychoeducation
description: Therapist provides clear, tailored information about CBT principles, diagnosis, symptom mechanisms, and treatment rationale to foster patient understanding, reduce stigma, and empower self-management.

goal.objective: Improve patient insight and understanding of problems, CBT approach, and rationale for intervention.

success_levels.ideal: Patient accurately understands and can explain CBT concepts relevant to their case, increasing motivation.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient receives relevant information and shows partial understanding or curiosity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient misunderstands or rejects CBT explanations or shows increased confusion.

goal.reward_hint: Patient asks informed questions, discusses new insights, or shows increased engagement following psychoeducation.

states: Beginning phase or with new topics/interventions
When patient displays misconceptions, unrealistic expectations, or confusion about therapy or their symptoms
Following assessment when introducing the CBT model

micro_actions.name: Deliver Tailored CBT Information
micro_actions.description: Therapist explains relevant CBT principles, treatment rationale, and mechanisms of symptoms in clear, patient-specific language.
states: When introducing CBT approach
Patient asks about treatment rationale or misunderstands therapy logic

micro_actions.name: Use Metaphors and Analogies
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses relatable metaphors or analogies to clarify complex CBT concepts or normalize patient experiences.
states: Patient displays difficulty grasping CBT principles
Concepts like 'learning from experiments' or 'perspective shifting' need clarification

micro_actions.name: Provide Psychoeducation on Normal Reactions
micro_actions.description: Therapist describes the normalcy of distressing thoughts, emotions, or bodily sensations to reduce self-stigma and shame.
states: Patient expresses confusion, shame, or worry about their experiences
Discussing symptom mechanisms or ‘normal’ responses

micro_actions.name: Check for Understanding and Invite Questions
micro_actions.description: Therapist actively asks about the patient’s understanding, encourages questions, and clarifies misconceptions after psychoeducational statements.
states: Immediately after providing information or explaining CBT concepts

micro_actions.name: Reinforce Psychoeducation with Visuals or Handouts
micro_actions.description: Therapist offers written summaries, handouts, flashcards, or diagrams to reinforce psychoeducation points and aid retention.
states: Whenever describing complex models
Patient has memory or attention difficulties

name: Collaborative Identification of Target Cognitions and Behaviors
description: Therapist and patient jointly identify problem-maintaining thoughts, beliefs, assumptions, and behaviors as focal points for intervention, ensuring relevance and ownership.

goal.objective: Develop a prioritized list of key cognitions and behaviors to target in therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient agree on a clearly defined set of target cognitions/behaviors directly linked to distress or dysfunction.
success_levels.acceptable: Therapist identifies some relevant targets; patient acknowledges their importance.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Targets remain vague or unrelated to the patient’s lived experience.

goal.reward_hint: Agreement and explicit list of priority targets is documented in session.

states: After case formulation, before intervention planning
When specific problematic beliefs or behaviors are evident and require clarification
At points where therapy focus needs realignment

micro_actions.name: Use Socratic Questioning to Elicit Problem Cognitions
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks targeted, open-ended questions to uncover underlying beliefs and assumptions driving distress or dysfunction in the patient's experience.
states: When patient describes distressing events, emotions, or maladaptive behaviors

micro_actions.name: Probe for Behavioral Patterns Related to Cognitions
micro_actions.description: Therapist queries about observable behaviors, safety behaviors, avoidance strategies, and their links to target beliefs during discussion.
states: Whenever patient reports problematic behaviors
Clarifying behavior-cognition links

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Generate and Clarify Target List
micro_actions.description: Therapist and patient jointly list and clarify mutually agreed upon cognitions and behaviors as key therapy targets.
states: After sufficient assessment and discussion of patterns

micro_actions.name: Explicitly Record and Review Targets in Session
micro_actions.description: Therapist documents selected target beliefs/behaviors (verbally or in writing/video/audio), reviews them with the patient for clarity and relevance.
states: Immediately after agreement on targets
When shifting focus in therapy

micro_actions.name: Elicit and Rate Belief Strength
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks the patient to numerically rate belief strength in each identified cognition, providing a baseline for intervention.
states: During target identification phase
Before interventions or behavioral experiments

name: Planning and Design of Behavioral Experiments
description: Therapist leads collaborative design of behavioral experiments (BEs) to test specific beliefs/predictions, challenge avoidance, or facilitate new learning, ensuring tailoring to individual needs and capabilities.

goal.objective: Produce a feasible, relevant, and collaboratively agreed upon plan for behavioral experiments to test maladaptive cognitions and promote change.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient have a detailed plan for an experiment addressing critical beliefs, with clear predicted outcomes.
success_levels.acceptable: Experiment is loosely planned with intent to test target cognition, though some details may be missing.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No experiments are planned, or designs are irrelevant, unsafe, or un-agreed upon.

goal.reward_hint: Patient expresses commitment or curiosity about the experiment, and details are clearly identified.

states: Therapy sessions after target beliefs are identified
When patient is ready to move from discussion to experiential learning
Before exposure/interpersonal experiments designed to test avoidance or catastrophic predictions

micro_actions.name: Formulate Testable Predictions
micro_actions.description: Therapist helps the patient generate explicit, concrete predictions for what will happen during the planned experiment.
states: After experiment rationale is discussed
Before experiment execution

micro_actions.name: Specify Experiment Parameters and Variables
micro_actions.description: Therapist and patient jointly define critical experiment details—action to be taken, context, safety behaviors to avoid, parameters to control.
states: During planning of individual experiment
When detailing procedures and controls

micro_actions.name: Explicitly Rate Beliefs and Emotions Pre-Experiment
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts patient to rate the strength of their target beliefs, alternative perspectives, and emotional states before experiment execution.
states: Immediately prior to the experiment

micro_actions.name: Assess and Discuss Safety Concerns
micro_actions.description: Therapist checks for, discusses, and addresses patient fears, safety behaviors, and logistical/cultural/social concerns related to experiment planning.
states: During collaborative planning
Whenever patient expresses doubts or resistance

micro_actions.name: Agree on Experiment Type and Scope
micro_actions.description: Therapist and patient clarify the type (active, observational, hypothesis-testing, graded, role-play) and scope/limits for the experiment.
states: Any time a new experiment is designed

micro_actions.name: Document Experiment Plan
micro_actions.description: Therapist writes down or visually records the experiment rationale, target belief, prediction, parameters, and agreed steps for session reference.
states: At the conclusion of experiment planning

name: Execution of Behavioral Experiments and Structured Experiences
description: Therapist guides, facilitates, and sometimes models the patient’s participation in planned behavioral experiments or exposure tasks, either in-session or assigned as homework, with attention to safety and relevance.

goal.objective: Successfully engage the patient in the structured experience/experiment to generate direct evidence and learning.

success_levels.ideal: Patient actively participates, experiment proceeds as planned, and meaningful data for hypothesis testing is gathered.
success_levels.acceptable: Experiment is attempted with partial engagement; some learning occurs despite challenges.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Experiment is avoided, disrupted, or leads to adverse outcomes.

goal.reward_hint: Patient’s actions align with the planned experiment and outcome data are available for follow-up.

states: After experiment planning, before reflection or review
Patient is ready and willing to test beliefs ‘in vivo’ or through structured tasks
During exposure-based tasks or skills practice

micro_actions.name: Model and Coach Experiment Participation
micro_actions.description: Therapist demonstrates or participates in the experiment alongside the patient, or provides stepwise coaching to guide action execution.
states: Patient is anxious or reluctant to engage
During active in-session experiments

micro_actions.name: Encourage In-Session and Homework Practice
micro_actions.description: Therapist encourages patient to enact experiment actions both within sessions and as assigned homework for generalization.
states: After initial experiment
When increasing tolerance or generalization is needed

micro_actions.name: Monitor and Troubleshoot Obstacles in Real Time
micro_actions.description: Therapist attends to barriers or distress encountered, offers adaptive supports, reframes, or modifies steps to increase patient safety and engagement.
states: During experiment execution
Patient expresses discomfort, uncertainty, or avoidance

micro_actions.name: Prompt Dropping or Modification of Safety Behaviors
micro_actions.description: Therapist gently encourages the patient to refrain from or alter safety behaviors in order to optimize experiment learning value.
states: Experiments involving avoidance/safety routines
When patient is engaged in ritualistic behaviors

micro_actions.name: Facilitate Real-Time Rating of Anxiety and Beliefs
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts the patient to rate anxiety and beliefs during experiment execution to track changes and increase self-monitoring.
states: During any structured behavioral experiment or exposure

name: Observation and Data Gathering
description: Therapist and patient observe, record, and collect data on the outcomes of experiments, behaviors, emotional responses, and cognitions as they unfold, ensuring unbiased evidence gathering.

goal.objective: Provide objective data for evaluating the validity of beliefs and intervention effectiveness.

success_levels.ideal: Complete, unbiased observations and data capture relevant to initial predictions.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial data or observations recorded, sufficient for basic hypothesis testing.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No meaningful data gathered; observations are ignored or misinterpreted.

goal.reward_hint: Concrete observation records (written, verbal, behavioral) are available post-experiment.

states: Immediately after experiments or exposure sessions
When hypotheses need empirical data for evaluation
After a meaningful behavioral intervention

micro_actions.name: Prompt Systematic Observation and Recording
micro_actions.description: Therapist directs the patient to systematically observe, record, and rate their experiences, outcomes, and emotional reactions during and after experiments.
states: Directly after experiment or skill practice
When collecting baseline or post-intervention data

micro_actions.name: Facilitate Use of Diaries, Worksheets, or Logs
micro_actions.description: Therapist provides or prompts use of recording tools (e.g., diaries, logs, flashcards) to document observations and ratings.
states: During and post-experiment
When patient reports difficulty with recall or attention

micro_actions.name: Direct Patient to Rate Discrepancy between Prediction and Outcome
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks patient to explicitly rate and compare their predicted outcome versus actual experiences post-intervention.
states: Immediately following an experiment
When testing beliefs

micro_actions.name: Encourage External Validation via Survey or Feedback
micro_actions.description: Therapist structures involvement of significant others (e.g., surveys, observational feedback, conversations) to gather external or social data relevant to the key beliefs.
states: When beliefs or predictions involve other people’s responses
Experiments needing reality-testing

micro_actions.name: Listen for Bias in Perception, Memory, and Interpretation
micro_actions.description: Therapist actively listens and prompts correction of biased patient observations or interpretations to maximize data quality.
states: During post-experiment debrief
When reviewing gathered data

name: Reflection and Cognitive Restructuring
description: Therapist facilitates collaborative reflection on experimental outcomes, supports cognitive restructuring, encourages reconsideration of maladaptive beliefs, and fosters integration of new learning into core perspectives.

goal.objective: Modify dysfunctional beliefs and construct more adaptive perspectives based on evidence and reflection.

success_levels.ideal: Patient demonstrates meaningful cognitive change, adopts new adaptive beliefs, and recognizes evidence against old assumptions.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial reconsideration or tentative adoption of alternative perspectives occurs.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Beliefs remain unchanged or become more rigid despite evidence.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes changed or challenged beliefs and integrates experiment results.

states: After gathering data from behavioral experiments
When evidence contradicts or supports patient’s core beliefs
Following significant emotional or behavioral experiences in therapy

micro_actions.name: Joint Reflection on Experiment Outcomes
micro_actions.description: Therapist guides patient through a process of reflecting on experiment results, encouraging the patient to articulate discrepancies, insights, or surprises.
states: After any experiment or structured experience

micro_actions.name: Facilitate Explicit Cognitive Re-Evaluation
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts patient to re-rate target beliefs and alternative perspectives, guiding explicit re-evaluation of previously held assumptions.
states: During reflection and post-experiment discussion

micro_actions.name: Encourage Generation of Alternative Perspectives
micro_actions.description: Therapist collaboratively helps patient formulate and rate more adaptive alternative beliefs based on evidence and experience.
states: Post-experiment review
When beliefs have been shown inaccurate or unhelpful

micro_actions.name: Summarize Learning and Generalize Skills
micro_actions.description: Therapist helps patient summarize key learning points and draws connections to generalization or future application in new contexts.
states: Final stage of reflection after experiment review

micro_actions.name: Gently Probe for Resistance and Rationalizations
micro_actions.description: Therapist sensitively inquires about potential resistance, discounting of positive outcomes, or ongoing doubts, and encourages constructive challenge.
states: When patient resists cognitive change or dismisses evidence
During cognitive restructuring phase

name: Skills Training and Development of Coping Strategies
description: Therapist teaches, models, and reinforces adaptive skills (e.g., assertiveness, emotion regulation, self-monitoring, alternative coping) to address difficulties and enhance patient self-efficacy.

goal.objective: Increase the patient’s repertoire of effective coping and self-management strategies.

success_levels.ideal: Patient acquires and flexibly applies new skills across relevant life domains.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient learns basic skills and uses them in limited contexts.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No skill acquisition or skills not used beyond sessions.

goal.reward_hint: Patient reports or demonstrates use of new coping or behavioral skills outside therapy.

states: When functional or behavioral deficits are identified
Patient expresses a need for practical strategies
Preparation for new behavioral experiments or challenging situations

micro_actions.name: Model Adaptive Coping and Skills
micro_actions.description: Therapist demonstrates desired skills (e.g., assertive communication, distraction, emotion regulation) and provides structured guidance for patient rehearsal.
states: Skills training sessions
Immediately before or during experiment

micro_actions.name: Guide Role-Play and Behavioral Rehearsal
micro_actions.description: Therapist leads in-session role-play or rehearsal of target skills (e.g., assertiveness, coping, help-seeking, response prevention).
states: During practice of coping, assertiveness, or exposure skills

micro_actions.name: Coach Implementation of New Skills in Activities
micro_actions.description: Therapist instructs the patient on integrating new skills during behavioral tasks, homework, or in vivo experiments.
states: When patient prepares or executes structured experiences

micro_actions.name: Encourage Self-Monitoring and Reflection
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts patient to observe, record, and reflect on their use and effectiveness of coping strategies in different situations.
states: After skills practice
Reviewing homework or experiment outcomes

micro_actions.name: Reinforce and Reward Use of Adaptive Coping
micro_actions.description: Therapist provides verbal encouragement, highlights small achievements, and affirms adaptive changes to reinforce skill use.
states: Immediately after patient uses new skill
During skills generalization and habit formation

name: Relapse Prevention and Future Planning
description: Therapist and patient collaboratively develop strategies for relapse prevention, including identifying early warning signs, triggers, and formulating adaptive plans for future setbacks, ensuring maintenance of gains.

goal.objective: Equip patient with individualized plans to sustain change and respond effectively to future challenges.

success_levels.ideal: Clear, collaboratively-developed relapse prevention plan is in place and patient expresses confidence in its use.
success_levels.acceptable: Basic strategies are discussed, and patient shows some awareness of future risks.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No future planning; patient remains vulnerable to relapse with no strategies.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates awareness of relapse risks and proactive coping plans.

states: Following substantial progress in therapy
Before planned discharge or therapy ending
Patient expresses concern about setbacks or past relapses

micro_actions.name: Identify and Review Warning Signs and Triggers
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks the patient to list and describe personal early warning signs and triggers for relapse, using collaborative discussion and prompts.
states: Relapse prevention planning phase
When patient shares setback experiences

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Brainstorm Adaptive Responses
micro_actions.description: Therapist guides the patient in brainstorming and selecting concrete coping strategies and responses to anticipated triggers or setbacks.
states: During future planning
When patient expresses anxiety about possible relapse

micro_actions.name: Document and Review Relapse Prevention Plan
micro_actions.description: Therapist records the prevention strategy, reviews it with the patient, and encourages active contribution and ownership.
states: Before therapy ends or transitions
Upon achievement of significant therapy milestones

micro_actions.name: Rehearse Skills and Coping Strategies for High-Risk Situations
micro_actions.description: Therapist conducts role-play, simulation, or rehearsal of coping skills specifically for handling high-risk or relapse-prone situations.
states: When reviewing past setbacks
When preparing for anticipated difficult events

micro_actions.name: Facilitate Patient Reflection on Past Relapses and Learning
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts reflection on previous relapse experiences, emphasizes learning, and helps patient extract principles for future prevention.
states: When patient discusses prior failed attempts or challenges
During relapse review stage
